newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil complex closes off, gasoline hardest hit.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil complex closes off, gasoline hardest hit.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil and refined products closed sharply lower, with gasoline prices hardest hit, amid a correction of the oil complex following a recent price run up, traders said.
"We are in the midst of a correction to relieve some of the overbought condition we are in technically," said Tom Bentz, a trader with ING Derivatives.

September unleaded gasoline closed down 1.60 cents to 61.62 cents a gallon Monday. All three legs of the oil complex hit contract highs in the prompt months last week, but profit-taking firmly took hold on Friday, traders said.
With a U.K. holiday closing the International Petroleum Exchange in London on Monday, volume was thin, exaggerating price moves, traders said.

Gasoline fell as much as 2.72 cents to an intraday low of 60.50. Selling was accelerated by news that Tosco Corp came one step closer to re-opening its 172,000 barrel-per-day Marcus Hook, Pa. refinery after it reached a tentative labor pact with the union which represents the refinery's workers.
October crude closed down 34 cents to $21.62 a barrel and September heating oil closed down 0.96 cent to 61.03 cents a gallon.
Historically low inventories kept heating oil's intermonth spreads tight and prices backwardated. More expensive front months held back players from placing heat in storage, traders said.
Meanwhile, October crude's downside was limited by traders buying crude and selling gasoline in a reverse crack spread play, traders said.
Traders were split as to whether most of the correction had run its course.
"Crude oil could correct back to $20.90," said Rita Beale, an analyst with Fimat USA Futures.

Depending on how the market responds to inventory numbers to be released by the American Petroleum Institute due out late tomorrow, Beale said the correction could end this week or continue for the next two weeks.
ING's Bentz said prices of the oil complex could move sideways tomorrow. The focus may turn to the momentum of price change rather the value of prices themselves, Bentz said.
"Maybe we need a little more of a time correction in which you could see just a sideways market tomorrow which further corrects the momentum indicators," Bentz said.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, +1 212-859-1761
